@graph.name: Do we need an OroCommerce alternative before chefs can reorder by voice?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your storefront, catalogs and approval rules stay as they are. The change is for a restaurant whose chef calls your desk today: that chef now says the reorder aloud in our app and goes over every item before it reaches you.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than OroCommerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only at one narrow job: a short restaurant reorder from a chef happier saying it than shopping for it. OroCommerce does far more, from corporate accounts to payments, so we run alongside it and are not an OroCommerce alternative.

@graph.name: Oro's SmartAgent already accepts voice. What does your app add?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a real overlap. On the Enterprise edition, a buyer signed in to your store can ask SmartAgent, by voice or in writing, to check stock or place a reorder. If restaurants on your store use SmartAgent, keep it. Ours is a separate phone app built only around each restaurant's regular items: the chef just talks, then looks over what the app lists and fixes anything wrong before it goes, with no storefront to open.

@graph.name: Is it linked to OroCommerce? Will someone here still type these orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: The two are separate, nothing joins them out of the box, and you get support for each from its own company. By email, your office receives a file of the reorder as sent, so nobody answers a call, notes it down and reads it back; someone enters it from a finished list the chef approved. Through EDI or the API, it may load into OroCommerce or your ERP without retyping, provided either system is built to take such orders, which we check together in the demo. OroCommerce runs the store, and your ERP remains the system of record for customer accounts, inventory and billing. Our side holds the order guide for every restaurant, with its prices, plus the reorders that come through the app. A chef who phones instead still gets no order number from us.

@graph.name: Some of our customers are groups with approval rules. Does this change that?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Groups that need sign-offs, budgets and several logins keep ordering in OroCommerce, where those rules live. We made our app for the restaurant where the chef decides what to order and sends it.

@graph.name: Is OroCommerce a fit for foodservice distributors at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be. Oro sells to many kinds of distributors, and food distributors run it: one family-owned foodservice distributor in Ohio had an integrator add order guides and cut-off times for its restaurant customers. If your store works for the accounts on it, keep it, and add us for chefs who prefer the phone.

@graph.name: How soon can we start, and how is pricing set?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup is 24 to 48 hours for most distributors, with nothing in OroCommerce touched. You give us the items each restaurant tends to buy, most often in a spreadsheet exported from your system. From that we build the guides in our admin, then open an account for every restaurant. Each chef adds the app to their phone, and at most restaurants the first reorder goes out that same day. Oro explains that its license is priced on the value of goods sold through the store and offers a free Community Edition, but quotes its Enterprise pricing; we quote ours for each distributor too. An OroCommerce replacement would mean building a new store, which Oro's own FAQ puts at about six months on average, while adding us keeps yours as it is.
